careful.identity: Python module `refcode` for register reference codes like GB-0042/3/7a: a two-letter country, hyphen, four-digit repository, then up to 5 levels (number 1-9999 plus optional lowercase letter). Public: CodeError(ValueError); class Code(country, repository, levels=()) with levels a tuple of (int, letter) pairs, value-equal, hashable, totally ordered, repr Code('text'); parse(text)->Code; show(code)->canonical str; depth(code)->int; parent(code)->Code or None; is_ancestor(a,b)->bool; common(a,b)->Code or None; next_sibling(code)->Code; children(code,count)->list of Code. MAX_DEPTH=5.
careful.laws: parse accepts only str (else CodeError). It strips outer whitespace and uppercases the country; nothing else is repaired (lowercase letters stay required in levels, no leading zeros, no inner spaces). Refuse: bad head, repository 0000, more than 5 levels, any level not matching [1-9]\d{0,3}[a-z]?, so 0 and 10000 are refused, and an empty level such as trailing slash is refused. show round-trips parse. Ordering is by the tuple (country, repository, levels); levels compare by number, then letter, with no letter before 'a'. A code sorts before all codes beneath it. is_ancestor is strict and requires the same repository. common returns the deepest shared prefix, which may be the repository itself, or None across repositories. next_sibling: 7->8, 7a->7b; refuses a repository, z, and 9999. A lettered code keeps its number and moves the letter only. children numbers from 1 with no letters; refuses at depth 5 and a count outside 0..9999.
careful.exemplars:
parse(' gb-0042/3/7a ') -> Code('GB-0042/3/7a')
parse('GB-0000') -> CodeError
parse('GB-0042/03') -> CodeError
parse('GB-0042/1/2/3/4/5/6') -> CodeError
parse('GB-0042/7A') -> CodeError
next_sibling(parse('GB-0042/7a')) -> Code('GB-0042/7b')
next_sibling(parse('GB-0042/9999')) -> CodeError
parse('GB-0042/7') < parse('GB-0042/7a') -> True
parse('GB-0042/7a') < parse('GB-0042/8') -> True
common(parse('GB-0042/1/2'), parse('GB-0042/3')) -> Code('GB-0042')
careful.development: Use two compiled regexes and a tuple-based key for eq, ordering and hash, with functools.total_ordering. Represent levels as (int, str) pairs. Keep functions pure, building new Code objects instead of mutating.

cheap.identity: Reference-code unit for a small register. Models codes like GB-0042/3/7a: a repository (two ASCII letters, hyphen, four digits, not 0000) followed by up to five levels, each a number 1-9999 with an optional lowercase letter. Public names: CodeError(ValueError); Code(country, repository, levels=()) with equality, total ordering, hashing and repr; parse(text)->Code; show(code)->canonical str; depth(code)->int; parent(code)->Code or None; is_ancestor(a,b)->bool; common(a,b)->Code or None; next_sibling(code)->Code; children(code,count)->list of Code; MAX_DEPTH=5.
cheap.laws: parse strips outer whitespace, splits on '/', requires head match of two letters, hyphen, four digits; country uppercased, repository kept as text; repository '0000' refused; more than 5 levels refused; each level must match number starting 1-9 of up to four digits plus optional single lowercase letter; non-str input refused; every refusal raises CodeError with its message. Levels stored as (int, letter-string) tuples; letter empty string when absent. show joins with '/' and writes levels as number then letter. parent drops last level; repository has none. is_ancestor is strict, same country and repository, shorter and prefix-matching. common returns deepest shared-prefix code, None across repositories; a code is its own common. next_sibling: repository refused; letter increments (7a->7b), 'z' refused; no letter increments number (7->8), 9999 refused; without letter, 7 goes to 8 not 7a. children: at depth 5 refused; count outside 0-9999 refused; returns numbered children from 1 with no letters. Order: compare country, repository, then levels lexicographically; a prefix sorts before its extensions; within a level compare number then letter, with no letter before 'a'. Equality and hash follow the same key.
cheap.exemplars:
parse(' gb-0042/3/7a ') -> Code('GB','0042',[(3,''),(7,'a')])
show(parse('gb-0042/3/7a')) -> 'GB-0042/3/7a'
parse('GB-0000') -> CodeError
parse('GB-0042/0') -> CodeError
parse('GB-0042/1/2/3/4/5/6') -> CodeError
next_sibling(parse('GB-0042/7a')) -> GB-0042/7b
next_sibling(parse('GB-0042/7')) -> GB-0042/8
next_sibling(parse('GB-0042/7z')) -> CodeError
parent(parse('GB-0042')) -> None
common(parse('GB-0042/3/7a'), parse('GB-0042/3/9')) -> GB-0042/3
children(parse('GB-0042/3'), 2) -> [GB-0042/3/1, GB-0042/3/2]
cheap.development: Use a small frozen-style class with a single key tuple driving eq, hash and lt via total_ordering. Put the regexes at module level, build parse with a single split and per-part match. Keep letter as empty string rather than None so tuples compare cleanly. Implement helpers as plain functions over the immutable fields.
